Cape Town International Airport Upgrade: R10 Billion Investment Plan

2026.03.25 8 min read Scott Huang | Business Development Property Investment

While global investors search for the next undervalued opportunity, the South African government has already answered with concrete action. In January 2026, the Airports Company South Africa (ACSA) officially announced: it will invest more than R10 billion over the next five years to comprehensively upgrade Cape Town International Airport (CPT). This is not only the largest airport infrastructure investment in South African history, but also opens a window of opportunity for astute property investors.

Why Does Cape Town Airport Warrant a R10 Billion Investment?

Cape Town International Airport is not only South Africa's gateway but also the aviation hub for the entire Southern African region. According to official ACSA data, the airport handled 11.4 million passengers in 2024, up 12% from pre-pandemic levels. As international tourism fully recovers, existing terminal facilities are nearing capacity, making the upgrade urgent.

Core Elements of the Upgrade Plan

According to the CPT Airport Development Plan 2026-2030 released by ACSA in January 2026, the R10 billion will be allocated to:

  • International terminal expansion: Increase floor area by 30%, raising annual passenger capacity from 14 million to 20 million
  • Runway system upgrade: Extend the main runway to 4,500 metres, accommodating large aircraft such as the A380
  • Smart airport development: Introduce biometric clearance, self-service baggage drop, and AI-powered flight scheduling
  • Green airport certification: Solar power supply, rainwater harvesting, and carbon neutrality by 2030
  • Seamless transport connectivity: Expand the MyCiTi rapid bus network, linking Cape Town city centre with the airport rail line
"This investment is not merely to meet current demand, but to lay the foundation for the next 20 years of growth. Cape Town will become Africa's gateway of choice to the world." — ACSA CEO Lukhona Nxasana

How Does the Airport Upgrade Move the Property Market?

The impact of infrastructure investment on real estate is a universal economic principle. According to Airports Council International (ACI) research, every US$1 invested in airport infrastructure generates approximately US$3.50 in regional economic benefits. This effect is directly reflected in property values.

Spillover Effect: The Logic of Property Value Growth Nearby

The employment growth, commercial activity and transport convenience brought by the airport upgrade will directly lift property values in surrounding areas. Data from Invest Cape Town shows that airport upgrades of a similar scale typically drive property price increases of 10-30% within a 15-25 km radius over 3-5 years.

Employment Dividend: Rental Demand from 15,000 New Jobs

ACSA estimates that the airport upgrade will directly create approximately 15,000 construction-related jobs. Combined with indirect stimulation of logistics, tourism and hospitality industries, the total employment effect will reach 30,000 positions. This means many professionals will need housing near the airport, creating stable rental demand.

For investors, this means:

  • A stable source of rental income (engineers, project managers, technical staff)
  • Low vacancy protection (long-term corporate leases)
  • Capital appreciation potential (demand drives up prices)

Three Key Areas Investors Should Watch

Based on the airport upgrade plan and transport convenience, the following areas merit close attention from investors:

1. Somerset West — A Top Choice for the Middle Class

Located approximately 20 km southeast of the airport, about a 25-minute drive. It is one of Cape Town's most important suburbs, with quality schools, shopping centres and natural scenery. The employment growth from the airport upgrade will directly boost rental demand here. Current average prices are around ZAR 18,000-25,000/m², with an expected 15-20% appreciation potential between 2028 and 2030.

2. Stellenbosch — A Premium Investment Target

Located about 35 km from the airport, it is South Africa's premier university town and wine region. Properties here hold not only residential value but also collectible value. The increase in international flights after the airport upgrade will drive business travel and international buyer demand. Heritage homes and estate-grade properties are scarce resources with enormous appreciation potential.

3. Bellville — A Commercial Rental Hotspot

Just a 15-minute drive from the airport, it is Cape Town's commercial and educational centre. The Tygerberg campus and several corporate headquarters are located here, forming a stable white-collar rental market. The airport upgrade will further strengthen Bellville's position as a regional business hub, with continued growth in demand for business apartments and serviced residences.

Frequently Asked Questions FAQ

When will the Cape Town Airport upgrade be completed?
According to official ACSA announcements, the Cape Town International Airport upgrade is scheduled for phased completion by 2030. The first-phase terminal expansion began construction in 2025 and is expected to be completed and operational in 2028. After the full upgrade, annual passenger capacity will rise from 14 million to 20 million.
How will the airport upgrade affect surrounding property prices?
According to research by Airports Council International (ACI), airport infrastructure investment typically drives property appreciation within a 15-30 km radius. Areas around Cape Town Airport such as Somerset West, Stellenbosch and Bellville are projected to see 10-25% property price growth between 2028 and 2030. This appreciation stems mainly from employment growth, commercial activity and improved transport convenience.
How can Taiwanese investors purchase property in Cape Town?
Taiwanese investors can work through DingYao Advisory with South African partner Crestline Advisory. Investment funds are held in a lawyer-held TPFA trust account and released to the developer in instalments per the contract. Funds are deposited directly into the investor's Standard Bank Wealth private banking account, never passing through the advisory company. The bank only releases funds on instruction once investor authorisation is obtained and the project reaches contractual milestones. Fully compliant with FICA anti-money-laundering regulations.
How many jobs will the airport upgrade create?
According to official ACSA estimates, the Cape Town Airport upgrade will directly create approximately 15,000 construction-related jobs, including engineers, construction workers, project managers and technical staff. Combined with indirect stimulation of logistics, tourism, hospitality and retail industries, the total employment effect will exceed 30,000 positions. These jobs will be released progressively between 2025 and 2030, providing stable rental demand for the surrounding property market.
